correctness.rationale: Characteristic-polynomial equality forces det(h)=1 and tr(xh)=tr(x). Applying it to h^{-1}=tr(h)I-h gives (tr(h)-2)tr(x)=0. For nonzero tr(x), all h are trace-two unipotents and closure under products forces all rank-one nilpotent parts onto one line. For tr(x)=0, the traceless parts lie in the two-dimensional trace-orthogonal plane V; the alternating form tr(xyz) is nondegenerate and group multiplication makes their span totally isotropic, hence one-dimensional. The determinant-one units in F_q[I,y] then have sizes 2q, q-1, q+1 according to y^2, and the nilpotent case gives the exact equality pair. The argument uses odd characteristic exactly where division by two and trace-form nondegeneracy are needed.
